gloss: setting a question; posing a problem

definitions.gloss: setting a question; posing a problem; giving a quiz
definitions.explanation: The act of creating and presenting questions or problems, especially in exams, quizzes, or competitions.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}が{問題|もんだい}を{出題|しゅつだい}する。
{出題|しゅつだい}{範囲|はんい}は{教科書|きょうかしょ}の3{章|しょう}までです。
examples.english: The exam covers up to chapter 3 of the textbook.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{入試|にゅうし}では{難|むずか}しい{問題|もんだい}が{出題|しゅつだい}されたらしい。
examples.english: Apparently difficult questions were set in this year's entrance exam.

notes:
The act of creating and presenting exam questions. Composed of {出|しゅつ} (put out) + {題|だい} (topic, question). Very common in academic and testing contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出題|しゅつだい}{範囲|はんい}: scope of the exam
- {出題|しゅつだい}{傾向|けいこう}: question trends/patterns
- {出題|しゅつだい}{者|しゃ}: question setter
- {出題|しゅつだい}{形式|けいしき}: question format
- {出題|しゅつだい}する: to set questions

CONTRAST:
- {出題|しゅつだい}: setting questions (examiner's side)
- {解答|かいとう}: answering questions (test-taker's side)
- {回答|かいとう}: responding, replying (broader — surveys, questionnaires)
